I got my degree in a particular field (I don't like to give out too much specific info, so I won't mention which one). I took an internship in my field which led to some opportunities and some plans for the future. I got a university certification to do some specific work in this field, and went on to complete a large portion of graduate coursework, with every intention of finishing a PhD and becoming a professor so I could do research in my area of interest. I thought that this would be my way to do some real good for the world, since I had some well-developed ideas for the type of research I thought was important, useful, and under discussed.

However, more and more of my classes seemed to become less and less academically rigorous, while introducing more social issues that didn't seem particularly relevant. Some of these were SJW-type issues, such as racial and gender ratios among researchers and students, sexual-orientation issues among people affected by our work, and so on. I considered myself fairly liberal at the time, and thought I was among like-minded thinkers, so I felt comfortable bringing up my problems about this direction that my university was taking. However, in conversation I was largely just written off as a racist/sexist/homophobe (while saying nothing against any of these demographics), and in writing I was largely ignored.

I started to really realize that this was a problem around the same time that the police department for the University decided to stop using race in the description of criminal suspects on campus, as it was largely targeting black people. One of the tenured professors in my department ended up being the major player who brought this demand to the police and campaigned for it to be policy.

I was bewildered by the whole situation. Even more so when I couldn't find anyone in the department who was both against this and willing to speak about it. I've never been one to hold my tongue well, so I decided to take a break to figure things out and then change universities, rather than lose my position and fuck my career by telling the truth too loudly.

So I didn't go back. I didn't get a doctorate, I was never a professor, I didn't get grants to do great research; all I got was loan debt. But I got out of Seattle, got a normal job, surrounded myself with a sane community, and am much happier now.
